extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology from primary XML/PDF figures and methods; direct mechanisms are limited to assays actually performed in this paper.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: ΔM3 and ΔM4 against Candida albicans yeast cells
mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM evidence supports peptide-associated C. albicans cell-surface damage and leakage after treatment under the tested planktonic conditions.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Supports cell-surface damage/leakage in the tested assay; it is not a full molecular target assignment.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: ΔM3 and ΔM4 against mature Candida albicans biofilm
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Rhodamine G6 efflux and Sytox Orange assays support membrane permeabilization in mature C. albicans biofilm, with ΔM4 active at lower concentrations than ΔM3.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Evidence is concentration- and assay-context specific; no single membrane pore model is assigned.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: ΔM3 and ΔM4 in Candida albicans mature biofilm
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Metacaspase staining, ROS detection, and antioxidant gene-expression assays support oxidative-stress and pro-apoptotic response context in mature biofilm.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Supports stress/apoptotic-response association after peptide exposure; it does not prove a single upstream molecular target.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: ΔM3 and ΔM4 in Candida albicans mature biofilm
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Mitotracker and Fura-2 assays support altered mitochondrial activity and intracellular Ca2+ mobilization after peptide treatment.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanistic context is downstream cellular response, not direct peptide-target binding evidence.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: ΔM3 and especially ΔM4 against Candida albicans hyphae and biofilm phenotypes
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Microscopy, hyphal-length measurement, qPCR, and XTT biofilm assays support inhibition of filamentation and biofilm formation phenotypes.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Phenotypic inhibition is not promoted to a direct molecular mechanism without the direct assays above.
